summary: The note describes how remote work, which grew during the pandemic and has persisted, is driving urban decentralization and reshaping real estate demand. Suburbs and rural areas are seeing higher demand, investment and new developments, while urban office space is being redesigned for hybrid use. It also covers demographic shifts, concerns about overheating in non-urban markets, and the need for government oversight.
one_line: Persistent remote work is pushing real estate demand, investment and development toward suburbs and rural areas while urban offices are redesigned for hybrid use.
key_facts: Globex Innovations, led by CEO Emily Martens, reported that 75% of its workforce continues to work remotely, at least part-time.
A FutureNow Insights study released October 15, 2023 found over 60% of employees across sectors prefer working from home for most of their workweek.
Henderson & Blake reported a surge in November 2023 in inquiries for properties with extra space for home offices and communities with natural surroundings and lifestyle amenities.
Julia Henderson, a leading realtor at Henderson & Blake, said clients are seeking homes in less dense areas offering 'holistic environments conducive to remote work.'
On December 12, 2023, TechFuture Capital announced a $500 million investment in smart work hubs in suburban and rural areas.
Broadband infrastructure projects have accelerated, particularly in areas previously considered too remote for significant economic investment.
David Liu of UrbanWorks Properties said on January 5, 2024 that the firm is redesigning office spaces to be more flexible, with shared workspaces rentable for short-term projects or meetings.
Some speculate central business districts may drop in value due to reduced office demand, while others see opportunities for residential conversions or innovative commercial uses.
Remote workers' influx is driving up home pricing and demand in suburbs and exurbs, and subdivisions are adding features like integrated green spaces and neighborhood co-working facilities.
Sociologist Dr. Amelia Rivera said in a February 20, 2024 webinar that 'We're witnessing a historic reconfiguration of where and how the next generation is choosing to live and work.'
Travis and Associates, a mid-sized development company, broke ground on March 10, 2024 for a 'telecommuter town' outside Charlotte, North Carolina.
Concerns exist about market overheating in non-urban areas, and state and local governments are being called on to provide strategic oversight for responsible growth.
